 This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of Motor vehicle Act, 1988, praying to: a) Call for the records in MVC No.804/2014, on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Kundapura, Udupi District. b) Modify the Judgment and Award dated: 23.08.2016, passed in MVC No.804/2014, on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at, Kundapura, Udupi District and c) Grant such other relief or relief's as this Court may deem fit in the circumstances of the case.
 This Miscellaneous First Appeal, coming on for Final hearing, through Physical Hearing/Video Conferencing, this day,
the Court delivered the following:
 JUDGMENT

The present appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Court of the learned Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at, Kundapura, (hereinafter for brevity referred to as "the Tribunal"), in its judgment and award dated 23-08-2016, in M.V.C.No.804/2014.
2.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at, Kundapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The summary of the case of the claimant before the Tribunal was that, on the date 19-07-2014, at about 9:30 hours, while the claimant along with one Smt. Kamala who is also a claimant in M.V.C.No.803/2014 was walking on the side of the road, leading from Ampar- Kundapura and when they were near Jigar cross road at Amparu village, a Maruthi Swift Motor Car bearing registration No.KA-25/N-8706, being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and coming from Amparu side, dashed to both the claimants, due to which road traffic accident, both the present claimant and Smt. Kamala sustained injuries.
According to the claimant herein, she was shifted to Chinmayi Hospital, Kundapura, where she has taken treatment as an in-patient from the date 19-07-2014 to 23-07-2014.
She has also stated that she underwent a surgical operation and has not recovered from the injuries.

Smt. Prema Kulal vs Prashanth Shetty on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58534359/
2

The claimant has further stated that, at the time of the occurrence of the road traffic accident, she was working as a Coolie and earning a sum of `15,000/- per month, however, due to the injuries suffered by her, she is disabled and unable to pursue her avocation.
With this, she has claimed in total a compensation of a sum of `15,50,000/- from the respondents No.1 and 2, arraigning them as the owner and insurer of the alleged offending Motor Car respectively.
3. Upon service of notice, both the respondents appeared before the Tribunal through their counsels, however, it is only respondent No.2 which filed its statement of objections.
In its Statement of Objections, it denied the occurrence of the road traffic accident in the manner and as alleged by the claimant.
It specifically denied that the claimant sustained injuries, much less the one that are depicted by the claimant.
Further, denying the age, income and avocation and the alleged disability of the claimant, the respondent No.2 - Insurance Company prayed for rejection of the claim petition.

4. Before the Tribunal, the claimant got herself examined as PW-1 and got marked documents from Exs.P-1 to P-10 and also examined one more witness Dr. Dinesh kumar Shetty, an Orthopaedic Surgeon as PW-2, through whom, got marked two more documents as Exs.P-11 and P-12.

However,
on behalf of the respondents, neither any witness was examined nor any documents were got marked.
5.

After analysing the evidence and the materials placed before it, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation under the following heads with the sum shown against them:
Sl.
 Particulars Amount in `
 No.
 1 Pain and sufferings 30,000-00
2 Medical expenses, food and 17,790-00  nourishment, attendant and  conveyance charges  3 Loss of earning during the laid up 32,500-00  period
4 Disability 93,600-00  5 Loss of amenities 12,000-00  Total 1,85,890-00 6.

The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of a sum of `1,85,890/- with interest at the rate of `6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation of the entire amount, holding the owner and Insurer jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation.

It is against the said judgment and award passed Smt. Prema Kulal vs Prashanth Shetty on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58534359/
3

sentences.text: by the Tribunal, the claimant has filed this appeal, seeking enhancement of compensation.
7. The learned counsel for the appellant (claimant) is appearing physically before the Court.
On a memo filed by the learned counsel for the appellant, notice to Respondent No.1 (owner of the offending vehicle) is dispensed with vide order dated 24-11-2017.
Even though notice for the respondent No.2 (Insurance Company) was accepted by its panel counsel, but no vakalath was filed on behalf of the Insurance Company.
8. Records from the Tribunal are called for and the same are placed before this Court.
9. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant.
Perused the materials placed before this Court including the memorandum of appeal, impugned judgment and also the records of the Tribunal.

10. The present appeal being the claimant's appeal and the respondent Insurer having not preferred either cross-objection or a counter appeal, the question of occurrence of the road traffic accident on the date, time and place as alleged by the claimant and also the alleged rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle is not in dispute.

Further, the claimant got herself examined as PW-1, where in her examination-in-chief, she has reiterated the contentions taken up by her in her claim petition regarding the occurrence of the road traffic accident and the manner of occurrence of injuries sustained by her and also about her alleged disability.

In support of her contention, apart from examining one Dr. Dinesh Kumar Shetty, an Orthopaedic Surgeon as PW-2, she has also got produced and marked documents from Exs.P-1 to P-10, which inter alia includes the copies of the complaint, FIR, wound certificate, scene of offence panchanama, motor vehicle inspection report, rough sketch of the spot, charge sheet, disability certificate, which goes to establish the occurrence of the road traffic accident on the date, time and place as mentioned in the claim petition and the claimant sustaining injuries in the said accident, so also the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the alleged offending Motor vehicle in causing the said road traffic accident.
Thus, the only question that remains for consideration is, whether the claimant is entitled for any enhancement in the compensation awarded by the Tribunal in the matter.

11. The learned counsel for the appellant (claimant) in his argument submitted that, the claimant has sustained multiple injuries and was treated as an in- patient in the Hospital for considerable length of time, as such, the quantum of compensation awarded under all the heads including the head of pain and sufferings is on the lower side and liable to be enhanced.

He further submitted that even though the claimant has not produced any documentary proof about her income, still, the Tribunal was required to take the notional income at a sum of `8,500/- per month, which was prevailing for the relevant year, however, the Tribunal has considered a lesser income as the Smt. Prema Kulal vs Prashanth Shetty on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58534359/
4 notional income of the claimant.

entities.text: Smt. Prema Kulal vs Prashanth Shetty
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With this, he submitted that the appeal deserves to be allowed.

12. As observed in the order sheet dated 19-04-2023 in detail, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 Insurance Company who had accepted the notice for respondent No.2 Insurance Company has neither appeared and addressed his arguments in the matter nor even has filed his vakalath in the matter.
As such, it was taken that the respondent No.2 though was served, has not proceeded in the matter.

The evidence of PW-1 (claimant) that in the accident, she sustained multiple injuries is further corroborated by the Wound Certificate at Ex.P-2 and also by the evidence of PW-2 Doctor, who has clinically examined the claimant.

The Wound Certificate as well the evidence of PW-2 reveals that,
in the road traffic accident, the claimant sustained the following injuries:
(i) Trochantic fracture right hip- undisplaced (ii) laceration on the right ankle measuring 10X6 cm.
(iii) laceration on the forehead measuring 4 X 2 cm.
The injury No.1 was opined as grievous in nature and the other two injuries were opined as simple in nature.
According to PW-2 Orthopedic Surgeon, the claimant was admitted in their Hospital from the date 19-07-2014 to the date 23-07-2014 and she was treated conservatively and with skin traction.
Thus, the claimant must have suffered considerable pain on account of the injuries sustained by her.

Since it is considering the injuries and sufferings suffered by the claimant, the Tribunal has awarded a - 11 - compensation of a sum of `30,000/- towards pain and sufferings, I do not find any reason to modify the same.
14. The claimant, as PW-1 though deposed that she has incurred a sum of `40,000/- towards medical expenses, however, she could able to produce the medical bills worth to an extent of `12,792/- only.

It is after taking into consideration those medical bills, which were the actuals,
produced by the claimant at Ex.P-10, since the Tribunal has awarded a sum of `17,790/-,
considering her stay in the Hospital and requirement of an attendant and special diet, by awarding a sum of `3,000/- and `2,000/- towards them respectively, I do not find any reason to enhance the said amount.

15. The claimant has contended in her claim petition that at the time of the road traffic accident, she was working as a Coolie and was earning a sum of `15,000/- per month, however, in her deposition as PW-1, she has stated that she was earning a sum of `9,000/- per month.

Admittedly, except her Smt. Prema Kulal vs Prashanth Shetty on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58534359/
5 self-serving oral statement, there - 12 - is no other piece of evidence including any documents to corroborate her evidence regarding the income, as such, the Tribunal has decided to take the notional income of the claimant for the relevant year, however, in the said process, it has taken the notional income at a sum of `6,500/- per month, when in fact, for the relevant year, i.e. 2014, a large number of Motor Accident Claims Tribunal in the State were taking a sum of `8,500/- per month as the notational income.

entities.text: Smt. Prema Kulal vs Prashanth Shetty
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the income of the claimant for the relevant period is required to be taken at a sum of `8,500/- per month.

Towards loss of income during the laid up period, which laid up period, according to the Tribunal,
was five months, it has awarded a sum of `32,500/- computed at the rate of `6,500/- per month.

In view of the fact that now the notional income of the claimant is taken at an enhanced amount of a sum of `8,500/- per month, which is `2,000/- higher than what the Tribunal had taken earlier, the claimant is entitled for the differential amount - 13 - of `10,000/- (i.e. `2,000x5 months) as the enhancement under the said head.

16. The claimant has contended that due to the injuries sustained by her in the road traffic accident,
she is unable to continue her avocation.

In her support, apart from producing the Disability Certificate said to have been issued by PW-2 - Orthopaedic Surgeon and getting it marked at Ex.P-8,
she also got examined the said Dr. Dinesh Kumar Shetty, Orthopedic Surgeon at Chinmayi Hospital,
Kundapura, as PW-2.
The said witness stated that, due to the injuries suffered by her in the road traffic accident, the claimant was admitted and treated in their Hospital as an in-patient.

Claiming to have gone through the medical records and clinically examining the injured claimant, PW-2 Doctor has opined that the claimant was suffering with a disability of 12% to her right lower limb.
The Tribunal has taken the percentage of disability as applicable to the whole body at 8%.

Though the learned counsel for the appellant (claimant) contended that the - 14 - Tribunal ought to have taken the percentage of disability at 12% only, as assessed by the Doctor, I am of the view that, since 12% disability was confining to a particular right lower limb of the claimant, the Tribunal was justified in confining the said disability at 8% as applicable to the whole body of the claimant.
The Wound Certificate at Ex.P-2 shows the age of the claimant as 40 years as on the date of the occurrence of the road traffic accident, as such, the standard multiplier applicable is '15'.

Thus, the quantum of compensation towards loss of future income/disability would come to `1,22,400/-
(i.e.`8,500/-x12x'15'x8/100).

After deducting a sum of `93,600/- awarded by the Tribunal under Smt. Prema Kulal vs Prashanth Shetty on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58534359/
6 the said head, the claimant is entitled for the differential amount of a sum of `28,800/- as enhancement.

entities.text: Smt. Prema Kulal vs Prashanth Shetty
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. Towards loss of amenities, the Tribunal has awarded a compensation of a sum of `12,000/-.

Considering the nature of the injuries and the organ of the body which suffered the said injury, the alleged avocation - 15 - of the claimant and the circumstance of the case, I am of the view that the said quantum of compensation awarded deserves to be enhanced marginally by another sum of `8,000/-, thus making it in total a sum of `20,000/-.
18. Barring the above, the claimant is neither entitled for compensation under any other heads nor the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the existing heads deserves any further modification.
19. Thus, as analysed above, the claimant is entitled for a modified compensation as tabulated below:

Sl.
 Particulars Amount in `
 No.
 1 Pain and sufferings 30,000-00  2 Medical expenses, food and 17,790-00  nourishment, attendant and  conveyance charges
3 Loss of earning during the laid up 42,500-00  period
4 Disability/loss of future income 1,22,400-00  5 Loss of amenities 20,000-00  Total 2,32,690-00

Since the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal at a sum of `1,85,890/-
is in short by a sum of `46,800/-, for the said enhancement of a sum of - 16 - `46,800/- only, the impugned judgment and award deserves to be interfered with.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
